# Full analysis pipeline for retail Weekly_Sales dataset
# Columns expected:
# Store (nominal), Dept (nominal), Date, Weekly_Sales (numeric),
# IsHoliday.x (logical/boolean or factor), Temperature (numeric),

# -------------------------------
# 0. Setup: packages and helpers
# -------------------------------
required_pkgs <- c(
  "tidyverse", "lubridate", "skimr", "ggpubr", "broom", "fitdistrplus",
  "car", "moments", "nortest", "randomForest", "caret", "pROC", "vip",
  "gridExtra"
)

installed <- rownames(installed.packages())
for (p in required_pkgs) {
  if (!p %in% installed) {
    install.packages(p, dependencies = TRUE)
  }
}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(skimr)
library(ggpubr)
library(broom)
library(fitdistrplus)
library(car)

library(nortest)

set.seed(42)

# 1. Load data

# Update path if necessary
path <- "C:/Users/Anthony Morciglio/OneDrive/Documents/Work/Personal Projects/Portfolio/Retail Data Project";
data_path <- file.path(path, "combined_dataset_final.csv");

if (!file.exists(data_path)) {

df_raw <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Quick look at column names
cat("Columns in dataset:\n")

# 2. Clean & prepare data

df <- df_raw %>%
  # Standardize column names (optional)
  rename_with(~ str_replace_all(., "\\.", "_")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Parse dates (tries common formats; adjust format if needed)
    Date = parse_date_time(Date, orders = c("Ymd", "Y-m-d", "m/d/Y", "d/m/Y", "Y/m/d")),
    # Ensure categorical types
    Store = as.factor(Store),
    Dept = as.factor(Dept),
    Type = as.factor(Type),
    # Convert holiday flags (both variants) to logical/factor
    IsHoliday_x = case_when(
      !is.na(IsHoliday_x) ~ as.logical(IsHoliday_x),
      !is.na(IsHoliday_y) ~ as.logical(IsHoliday_y),
      TRUE ~ NA
    ),
    IsHoliday = coalesce(IsHoliday_x, IsHoliday_y),
    IsHoliday = if_else(is.na(IsHoliday), FALSE, IsHoliday),
    # Numeric conversions (some CSVs have them as text)
    Weekly_Sales = as.numeric(Weekly_Sales),
    Temperature = as.numeric(Temperature),
    Fuel_Price = as.numeric(Fuel_Price),
    CPI = as.numeric(CPI),
    Unemployment = as.numeric(Unemployment),
    Size = as.numeric(Size),
    # Time features
    Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    Year = year(Date),
    Quarter = quarter(Date),
    DayOfWeek = wday(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE),
    # Season: Northern hemisphere convention
    Season = case_when(
      Month %in% c("Dec", "Jan", "Feb") ~ "Winter",
      Month %in% c("Mar", "Apr", "May") ~ "Spring",
      Month %in% c("Jun", "Jul", "Aug") ~ "Summer",
      Month %in% c("Sep", "Oct", "Nov") ~ "Fall",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Season = factor(Season, levels = c("Winter", "Spring", "Summer", "Fall")),
    Type = as.factor(Type),
    IsHoliday = as.factor(IsHoliday)
  )

# 4. Distribution fitting & diagnostics

# We'll attempt to fit common distributions for Weekly_Sales and Temperature.
# Weekly_Sales: candidate log-normal, gamma, normal (often right-skewed)
# Temperature: often approximately normal (seasonal)
library(fitdistrplus)

fit_dists <- function(x, varname) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  cat("Fitting distributions for:", varname, "\n")
  # transform if necessary
  if (min(x) <= 0) {
    # for lognormal/gamma, need positive; shift if necessary
    shift <- abs(min(x)) + 1e-6
    x_pos <- x + shift
  } else {
    shift <- 0
    x_pos <- x
  }
  fits <- list()
  # try normal
  fits$norm <- tryCatch(fitdist(x, "norm"), error = function(e) NULL)
  fits$lnorm <- tryCatch(fitdist(x_pos, "lnorm"), error = function(e) NULL)
  fits$gamma <- tryCatch(fitdist(x_pos, "gamma"), error = function(e) NULL)
  # compare with gofstat
  gof <- lapply(fits, function(f) if (!is.null(f)) gofstat(f) else NULL)
  return(list(fits = fits, gof = gof, shift = shift))
}

# Example for Weekly_Sales
ws_fit <- fit_dists(df$Weekly_Sales, "Weekly_Sales")
# Example for Temperature
temp_fit <- fit_dists(df$Temperature, "Temperature")

# Print AIC/BIC if available
if (!is.null(ws_fit$fits$lnorm)) {
  cat("Weekly_Sales fit AICs: \n")
  print(sapply(ws_fit$fits, function(x) if(!is.null(x)) x$aic else NA))
}

# Plot histogram with fitted curves for Weekly_Sales
plot_fitted <- function(x, fit_list, shift = 0, main = "Variable") {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  df_plot <- data.frame(x = x)
  p <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = x)) +
    geom_histogram(aes(y = ..density..), bins = 60, fill = "#d3d3d3", color = "black", alpha = 0.6) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = paste("Histogram and fitted densities:", main), x = main, y = "Density")
  # add fitted densities if present
  xseq <- seq(min(x), max(x), length.out = 1000)
  if (!is.null(fit_list$norm)) {
    params <- fit_list$norm$estimate
    p <- p + stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = params["mean"], sd = params["sd"]), color = "blue", size = 1)
  }
  if (!is.null(fit_list$lnorm)) {
    params <- fit_list$lnorm$estimate
    # remember shift
    p <- p + stat_function(fun = function(v) dlnorm(v + shift, meanlog = params["meanlog"], sdlog = params["sdlog"]), color = "red", size = 1)
  }
  if (!is.null(fit_list$gamma)) {
    params <- fit_list$gamma$estimate
    p <- p + stat_function(fun = function(v) dgamma(v + shift, shape = params["shape"], rate = params["rate"]), color = "darkgreen", size = 1)
  }
  return(p)
}

p_ws_fit <- plot_fitted(df$Weekly_Sales, ws_fit$fits, shift = ws_fit$shift, main = "Weekly_Sales")
p_temp_fit <- plot_fitted(df$Temperature, temp_fit$fits, shift = temp_fit$shift, main = "Temperature")

# 7.1 Confidence intervals for means (Weekly_Sales overall and by Type)
ci_mean <- function(x, conf = 0.95) {
  x <- na.omit(x)
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  s <- sd(x)
  se <- s / sqrt(n)
  alpha <- 1 - conf
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df = n - 1)
  lower <- m - t_crit * se
  upper <- m + t_crit * se
  tibble(n = n, mean = m, sd = s, se = se, lower = lower, upper = upper)
}

ci_overall <- ci_mean(df$Weekly_Sales)
cat("95% CI for overall Weekly_Sales mean:\n")
print(ci_overall)

ci_by_type <- df %>%
  group_by(Type) %>%
  summarise(ci = list(ci_mean(Weekly_Sales))) %>%

# 7.2 Hypothesis testing
# A) Does Type (A/B/C) affect Weekly Sales? Use ANOVA (plus Kruskal-Wallis if non-normal)
anova_mod <- aov(Weekly_Sales ~ Type, data = df)
anova_summary <- summary(anova_mod)
print(anova_summary)

# Check assumptions: normality of residuals and homogeneity of variances
resid_anova <- residuals(anova_mod)
print(length(resid_anova))
cat("Shapiro test for ANOVA residuals:\n")
print(shapiro.test(sample(resid_anova, 1000)))
cat("Levene Test for homogeneity:\n")
print(leveneTest(Weekly_Sales ~ Type, data = df))

# If ANOVA significant, Tukey HSD:
if (anova_summary[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1] < 0.05) {
  cat("ANOVA significant: performing Tukey HSD\n")
  print(TukeyHSD(anova_mod))
} else {
  cat("ANOVA not significant at alpha=0.05\n")
}

# Kruskal-Wallis as nonparametric alternative
kruskal_res <- kruskal.test(Weekly_Sales ~ Type, data = df)
print(kruskal_res)

# B) Holiday effect: two-sample t-test (Holiday vs Non-holiday)
# Check group sizes
table(df$IsHoliday)
holiday_group <- df %>% filter(IsHoliday == "TRUE") %>% pull(Weekly_Sales)
nonholiday_group <- df %>% filter(IsHoliday != "TRUE") %>% pull(Weekly_Sales)

# Non-equal variance t-test
t_test_holiday <- t.test(holiday_group, nonholiday_group, var.equal = FALSE)
print(t_test_holiday)

# Wilcoxon rank-sum test (nonparametric)
wilcox_res <- wilcox.test(holiday_group, nonholiday_group)
print(wilcox_res)

summary(anova_season)

### 9. Regression Modeling ---------------------------------------------

# Make sure column names are syntactically valid
names(df) <- make.names(names(df), unique = TRUE)

# Convert categorical predictors to factors
df$Store        <- as.factor(df$Store)
df$Dept         <- as.factor(df$Dept)
df$IsHoliday  <- factor(df$IsHoliday, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))
#df$IsHoliday.y  <- factor(df$IsHoliday.y, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE))
df$Type         <- as.factor(df$Type)

# Convert Date to a numeric "time index" (optional but helpful)
df$Date <- as.Date(df$Date)
df$TimeIndex <- as.numeric(df$Date - min(df$Date))  # days since start

# Select modeling columns
model_data <- df %>%
  dplyr::select(
    Weekly_Sales,
    Temperature, Fuel_Price, CPI, Unemployment,
    Store, Dept, IsHoliday, Type, Size, TimeIndex
  )

# Remove rows with missing values to avoid model errors
model_data <- na.omit(model_data);
model_df <- model_data;

# Fit the linear regression model
lm_model <- lm(Weekly_Sales ~ Temperature + Fuel_Price + CPI + Unemployment +
                 Store + Dept + IsHoliday + Type + Size + TimeIndex,
               data = model_data)

#summary_lm <- summary(lm_model)

# model_lm_long <- lm(log1p(Weekly_Sales) ~ Temperature + Fuel_Price + CPI + Unemployment + Store + Dept + IsHoliday + Type + Size + TimeIndex,
#                data = model_data);
#summary_model_lm_lomg <- summary(model_lm_long);

# Model diagnostics
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(lm_model)

# Variable importance via absolute t-values
importance <- abs(summary(lm_model)$coefficients[, "t value"])
importance_sorted <- sort(importance, decreasing = TRUE)
importance_sorted


# -------------------------------
# 10. Machine learning model: Random Forest for feature importance
# -------------------------------
# We'll predict Weekly_Sales (regression) using randomForest. For speed, sample if huge dataset
set.seed(42)
rf_df <- model_df %>% mutate(Weekly_Sales = as.numeric(Weekly_Sales))

# If dataset too big, optionally sample
if (nrow(rf_df) > 20000) {
  rf_df <- rf_df %>% sample_n(20000)
}

# Partition data
trainIndex <- createDataPartition(rf_df$Weekly_Sales, p = .8, list = FALSE)
train <- rf_df[trainIndex, ]
test  <- rf_df[-trainIndex, ]

# Train random forest
rf_formula <- as.formula("Weekly_Sales ~ Temperature + Fuel_Price + CPI + Unemployment + Size + Type + IsHoliday")
rf_model <- randomForest(rf_formula, data = train, ntree = 300, importance = TRUE, na.action = na.omit)
print(rf_model)

# Variable importance plot
png("RF_VariableImportance.png", width = 800, height = 600)
vip(rf_model)
dev.off()

# Predict on test set and compute RMSE
preds <- predict(rf_model, newdata = test)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((preds - test$Weekly_Sales)^2, na.rm = TRUE))
cat("Random Forest RMSE on test set:", rmse, "\n")

# Partial dependence for top features (if desirable)
top_vars <- names(sort(importance(rf_model, type = 1), decreasing = TRUE))[1:5]
cat("Top variables by RF (incMSE):\n")
print(top_vars)
